searchText: Is there a non-spec rationale post somewhere about ssz? Something explaining its properties? <@!213672586264051717> there is some nice rationale by <@!361447803194441738> here: https://ethereum.stackexchange.com/questions/74005/what-is-ssz-simpleserialize-and-why-was-it-developed I think my failure to include the merkleization aspect (hashing really) in the specs contributed significantly to people thinking SSZ was "meh", since my proposed change only includes the encoding/decoding part. Agenda for the next ACD is up, with YT stream link: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/224 Thanks <@!543900561460822016> for creating it 😄 An SSZ explainer above mentions scary numbers for merklezation, is it that bad (milliseconds)? <@!381789485777682434> merklization does take longer than simple one-off hashing of the bytes. Sure, but I’m curious about the concrete (and not Python) numbers Like, in the context of EIP2718 and the proposed SSZ usage there? That should be pretty easy to drum up (create) Something like taking the last million mainnet txns and comparing time to: - encode / decode (rlp vs ssz) - hash (keccak vs ssz) - extract parameters needed for signature verification And for context, probably good to compare these to the time it takes to verify the transaction signature for a sense of scale.

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content:
Something like taking the last million mainnet txns and comparing time to:

- encode / decode (rlp vs ssz)
- hash (keccak vs ssz)
- extract parameters needed for signature verification

And for context, probably good to compare these to the time it takes to verify the transaction signature for a sense of scale.
